name: Heavenly Stellar Secret Land
reason: Source term 'Heavenly Star Secret Realm' was localized as 'Heavenly Stellar Secret Land' for the Western fantasy setting, keeping the celestial imagery while avoiding the overused 'Realm' suffix.
description: The most important location in the seven divine kingdoms, a sealed secret land that the Union of Seven Divine Kingdoms can only enter with Soul Cores and a special ore harvested from giant leaves. In the source it is rumored to hold the Ancestral Dragon egg, drawing Divine Sea Realm experts. Zane joins the expedition into it during the Eps 844-961 arc.

name: Max
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Max' was chosen as a short, punchy name fitting the stocky, boisterous fellow-disciple archetype of source character Zhang Wuxian ('Fatty Zhang').
description: A stocky, hot-tempered Skyreach Sect disciple and one of Zane's earliest friends, part of the circle with Leo and the ill-fated Rex from the Razorwing campaign at the frontier fort (Eps 64+). His source counterpart Zhang Wuxian is the round-faced, well-connected outer-sect senior ranked seventh among outer disciples, known for brokering information and smoothing disputes. He remains in Zane's orbit through the homecoming arc around Ep 969, matching Zhang Wuxian's long source presence (chs 43-950).

name: Dark World
reason: The source location rendered variously as 'Asura Yin World' and 'Sifting Yin World' (both variants co-occur in the same source chapters) was unified and simplified to 'Dark World' for the Western fantasy register.
description: A remote, lawless world lying outside Alliance territory where many races gather, including the Nightfiend Clan. Zane travels there on Lincoln's invitation during the Eps 1095-1186 arc, navigating its backwater outposts with the secrets Lavender shared.

name: Corrupt Vitality
issues: Both 'Corrupt Vitality' (Eps 151+) and 'Nether Essence' (Eps 92-149, still used in Ep 387) localize aspects of the same source energy (Heavenly Demon True Qi / True Essence); the two terms coexist around Eps 387-388, so verify the intended distinction - possible split of one source entity into two localized names.
reason: The source's 'Heavenly Demon True Essence' (a variant rendering of the Heavenly Demon True Qi energy) was localized as 'Corrupt Vitality' to tie it to the show's canonical 'Vitality' energy system while conveying its dark, devouring nature.
description: The corrupted, purple-hued form of Vitality tied to Zane's innate devouring power, introduced by name in Ep 155 when he converts absorbed energy into it. Per the master sheet, Zane can absorb Vitality from defeated Nether Phantoms via his Shadow Vitality, creating massive clouds of purple Vitality that other cultivators cannot safely absorb. It remains a signature element of his combat style from Ep 151 through the Ep 1129 range, mirroring the source's spreading, net-forming Heavenly Demon True Essence.

name: Yates
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Yates' was chosen for the entitled young heir, and the surname 'Moon' was assigned to the Mo family (House Moon) to create a consistent family unit with his relative Ethan.
description: Heir of House Moon, son of James Moon and cousin to Ethan, a Fourth-Grade Adept and Eagle Peak inner disciple. Entitled and aggressive, he wields the Willow Spear and Willow Spear Art - matching source Mo Xiuyan, whose spear shaft is forged from the Wind Willow Tree Core. He antagonizes Zane in Eps 195-207, driven partly by envy over Ingrid's feelings for Zane.

name: Queen
issues: The surface form 'Queen' folds together at least two distinct figures: the Razorwing Queen (= source Blade Insect Queen) of Eps 67-74, and a different, humanoid Queen in late episodes (e.g. Ep 1161, ordering Lavender's Pool of Faith sealed). Do not merge these referents.
reason: Short title used in episodes for the Razorwing Queen, the localization of the source's 'Blade Insect Queen' commanding the insect swarms; the generic title was also reused for an unrelated late-arc monarch.
description: Primarily the Razorwing Queen (Eps 67-74): the winged, armored commander of the Razorwing swarm besieging the frontier fort, wielding crimson blades and directing the insects' retreats and attacks. Zane lures her away to save the squad, and her Core becomes a valuable trophy - mirroring the source's Blade Insect Queen who kills Yang Tai and whose crystal core Luo Zheng exchanges for points. Later episodes reuse 'the Queen' for a different ruler in the Ep 1161+ arc.

name: Chaotic Ocean of Stars
reason: Source term 'Chaotic Astral Ocean' was renamed 'Chaotic Ocean of Stars' for a more evocative Western fantasy register; the master sheet explicitly fixes this form over 'Chaotic Astral Ocean'.
description: A vast, storm-wracked forbidden sea realm east of the Central Domain that even False Tribulation Realm experts fear to enter. It holds Sacred Mount Lodestone and a celestial tomb of mist that hundreds of thousands have sought to breach. Zane is deposited at its bottom by teleportation array in the Ep 683+ arc, and its treasures recur from Ep 401 through Ep 1287.

name: Talent Tablet
reason: Source term 'Talent Stele' (also rendered 'Talent Monument') in the Tower of Sin was localized as 'Talent Tablet', keeping the meaning while using a more familiar English word.
description: A trial artifact associated with the Tower of Sin that tests entrants through mysterious trials, ranks them with particular titles, and in the source can even change one's talent. Crowds gather to watch the rankings shift whenever someone enters, and Zane undertakes its ultimate test during Eps 588-601.

name: Bob
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Bob' was chosen as a blunt, common name for the volatile noble-house bully, source Young Master Pei Hen; his family became House Pauling.
description: A Peak Adept antagonist of House Pauling with a notoriously explosive temper, feared enough that no one dares intervene when he is involved. He wields ice techniques (Icy Seal, Chillwater Drops) and squares off against Leo before being defeated by Zane at Emberfin Lake in Eps 183-188 - matching source Young Master Pei Hen of the seven noble families, who clashed with Meng Changjun and Luo Zheng at the Illusory Fish Pond.

name: Saint Morphen
reason: The source's Daoist title-name 'Daoist Master Dameng' ('Big Dream', also rendered Daoist Dameng / Daoist Big Dream) was localized as 'Saint Morphen', echoing Morpheus to preserve the dream motif while fitting the Western register.
description: One of the Cloud Hall's Elders, a master of spatial and illusionary arts and an unrivaled puppeteer. After reaching the Fusion Realm his control over puppets became absolute; he controls Zane's body through invisible threads of light from miles away, throwing him into sparring matches against Elite Hall disciples (Eps 411-421). Despite his doubts about Zane, he becomes an ambivalent protector during the Cloud Road treasure arc, mirroring Daoist Master Dameng's role in the Cloud Hall of the source.

name: Sacred Mount Lodestone
reason: The source's 'Divine Origin Magnetic Mountain' (also rendered Divine Magnetic Mountain / Divine Essencefused Mountain) was localized as 'Sacred Mount Lodestone', keeping the magnetic-mountain concept in plainer English.
description: A near-indestructible mountain from deep within the Chaotic Ocean of Stars whose five elements are so perfectly intertwined that no normal Law Power can refine it; a shard of it serves as the lodestone pre-qualifying test material containing seven Original Laws (Eps 459-461). Almost no one in history has refined one, but Zane later collects and forges a Sacred Mount Lodestone of his own with a secret technique, summoning it as a colossal crushing weapon in the Eps 1233+ battles, just as Luo Zheng collects the Divine Origin Magnetic Mountain in the source.

name: Killing Sword Mountain
reason: Source term 'Slaughter Sword Mountain' (also rendered Massacre/Slaughtering Sword Mountain) was localized as 'Killing Sword Mountain' for the Western fantasy register.
description: A legendary spiritual mountain that swordsmen who comprehend the Perfect Sword Essence may project their consciousness into, forming a contract with it. Climbers store their Malice there and vie to reach its peak; despite its fearsome reputation it is not physically large. Zane first enters and climbs it in Eps 298-303, and it recurs in his sword progression through Ep 1311.

name: Skycruiser
reason: Source term 'Flying Chariot' was localized as 'Skycruiser' to give the vessel a sleeker, more modern Western fantasy feel; the master sheet fixes this form over 'Armored Skycruiser' and 'Sky-carrier'.
description: An enormous flying vessel used by sects and noble houses for long-distance transport, rare and expensive enough that most people never ride one. Skycruisers ferry disciples to examinations and expeditions and even haul massive cargo like the stones for the Seven-Star Platform (Eps 31-351).

name: Silverspire
reason: The source's frontier stronghold 'White Emperor City' was renamed 'Silverspire' to fit the Western fantasy register while keeping the pale, towering imagery.
description: The strongest military outpost in The Crucible and an imperial army base, built into a mountainside so that its ramparts feel like a peak. It is the last bulwark between the massing demon army and the imperial capital, and Zane helps hold it against Demon Commanders during the Eps 116-146 war arc, mirroring the demon-war defense of White Emperor City in the source.

name: Keep
reason: Extraction artifact: the capitalized word is overwhelmingly the imperative 'Keep going/Keep them there' in dialogue, plus stray fragments of distinct locations (Dragon's Keep, Elysian Keep) that are separate entities; not a real standalone entity.

name: Alliance
reason: Source term 'Alliance' (the Upper World power bloc of the Heavenly Venerables, as in 'the Heavenly Venerables of the Alliance') was carried over directly as 'The Alliance'.
description: The dominant power bloc of the Upper World, encompassing the Thirteen Palaces and vast territory whose far edge takes Zane a month to reach. Its most powerful Supreme Lords watch the Passing the Torch trials, membership in it is a once-in-a-lifetime chance for warriors like Fenton, and lawless regions like the Dark World lie outside its jurisdiction (Eps 847-1320).

name: Grade-One Divine Weapon
reason: Source term 'first-grade divine artifact' was localized as 'Grade-One Divine Weapon' to fit the show's Divine Weapon grading system in the Upper World arcs.
description: The top common grade of Divine Weapon in the Upper World, so rare that the last one taken from the Groundstone Hall dome was about a hundred years prior. Zane claims one (the Thundergust sword) in Ep 1052, and elite warriors of the Thirteen Palaces and tenth-tier Holy Lands prize them; even a Grade-One blade can crack against truly ancient relics (Eps 1045-1316).

name: Divine Weapon
reason: Source term 'divine artifact' was localized as 'Divine Weapon' for the Upper World weapon class, distinct from the lower-world tier name 'Divine Arms'.
description: The weapon class of the Upper World arcs (Eps 961+), graded from Grade-One downward and ranked on the Cosmic Spirit Index. Even low-grade Divine Weapons from the Lower World pale beside Upper World armaments, and forces strong enough to swallow or twist a Divine Weapon mark the truly elite. It is a separate system from the lower-world weapon tiers (Spirit Weapon, Mythic Weapon, Sacred Arms, Divine Arms).

name: Gus
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Gus' was chosen as a casual, approachable name for the senior-brother figure, source Xian An.
description: A fellow disciple under the same master as Zane - 'a sort of big brother, not a blood one' - introduced in Ep 1193. Confident and hard to shake, he pursues and spars with Zane across Eps 1193-1223, testing his junior's talent, matching source Xian An, the shameless Senior Brother who guides Luo Zheng's choice of cultivation methods for crossing the Heavenly Dao.

name: Rylan
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Rylan' was chosen for the calculating mine boss, source Qiu Ren, whose chapter range (997-1003) aligns exactly with the episode arc.
description: The boss of a crew in the Soulbound Sect's mine (Eps 1020-1026), where the sect turns a blind eye to killings but Rylan still operates carefully. Unnerved by Zane's strength after Zane batters one of his men, he orders his crew to make Zane disappear quietly before confronting him directly.

name: Law of Causality
reason: Source term 'Karma Law' was localized as 'Law of Causality', a more precise English rendering of the cause-and-effect law concept.
description: One of the supreme categories of law in the universe, which not even a Supreme Lord can break. Upon attaining Supreme Lord status and bearing the Heavenly Destiny, one can forge divine power through the Law of Causality and gain millennia of extended life; its top tier is called the strongest law in the universe, and masters of it are nearly impossible to kill (Eps 751-1293).

name: Ace Talent
reason: The source title 'Chosen One' - a designation for warriors chosen by fate - was localized as 'Ace Talent' to read as a rank rather than a messianic label.
description: A title in the Illusion Battlefield arc (Eps 1274-1318) for elite warriors chosen by fate, whose strength outclasses even accomplished fighters of the same realm. Expedition groups prize having Ace Talents along, though even a Soul Sea Realm Ace Talent with a Divine Weapon can be helpless against the battlefield's worst dangers.

name: Grey
issues: Core usage (Eps 7-15) matches Grey Hawn; the extraction's stray late hit (~Ep 893) is likely the color word or an unrelated referent folded in by surface matching.

name: Grey Hawn
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name; 'Hawn' was chosen as a phonetic echo of the source surname Huang for the sycophantic family servant.
description: A flattering, well-connected servant of Zane's family's rivals whose wife was Master Andrew's nanny ever since Andrew's mother died - exactly matching source Huang Ge, whose wife was Luo Chengyun's wet nurse. Beaten to a pulp by Zane in Eps 7-8, he grovels before Andrew in Ep 10 begging for help against the boy, nursing his grudge through Eps 13-14.

name: Nether Essence
issues: Both 'Nether Essence' (Eps 92-149, still used in Ep 387) and 'Corrupt Vitality' (Eps 151+) localize aspects of the same source energy (Heavenly Demon True Qi / True Essence); the two terms coexist around Eps 387-388, so verify the intended distinction - possible split of one source entity into two localized names.
reason: The source's 'Heavenly Demon True Qi' (also rendered Heavenly Demon Genuine Qi / Heavenly Devil Qi) was localized as 'Nether Essence' to convey its dark, devouring nature in the Western fantasy register.
description: Zane's dark cultivation energy during the early demon-war arcs (Eps 92-149), surging through his veins like liquid lightning and powering his strikes and absorption tricks - he even twists an absorbed Apex Dragon with it. Its defining trait, as in the source's Heavenly Demon True Qi, is that it devours other energy, though it is a shadow compared to raw Life Force; the term resurfaces as late as Ep 387 alongside 'Corrupt Vitality'.

name: Thirty-Three Peaks
reason: The source's '33 peaks' / 'thirty-three peaks' of the Blue Cloud Sect was carried over directly as the 'Thirty-Three Peaks' of the Skyreach Sect.
description: The thirty-three divisions of the Skyreach Sect, whose hierarchy is reshaped by the great All Peaks Competition in which every peak participates (Eps 188-233). Misty Peak ranks last among them, and auxiliary peaks like Quenching Peak sit outside the official thirty-three; the peaks' members are fighters rather than smiths. The structure mirrors the Blue Cloud Sect's 33 peaks and Peak Competition in the source.
